llm.summary: The dominant macro fact this morning is that the Fed has flipped from cutting to possibly hiking: NY Fed's Williams explicitly refused to rule out back-to-back hikes and said higher rates are likely 'over time,' the dollar is at a 20-month high, JPMorgan is flagging 5%+ Treasury yields in 2027, and Ackman is warning a December hike could tip the US into recession. That repricing is colliding with a second shock — the Trump administration is readying a new wave of tariffs on China, the EU and Japan as soon as today — and with a third: the AI trade's reflexivity is now visible to everyone. Nvidia's 31% one-day melt-up on Jensen Huang's return gave back 5% the next session, Anthropic broke below its $83 IPO price for the first time, and the hardware tape is ugly (ADI -15.7%, HPE -14.6%, DELL -11.3%, CRDO -10.4%, MRVL -7.6% pre-market). Flows confirm the regime: Technology rotation score is -74 while Staples (+93), Health Care (+84), Real Estate (+74) and Utilities (+73) accelerate, and Value leads Growth by 89 points. The consumer is bifurcating but not broken — CB confidence printed 103.3 vs 92.5 expected, Best Buy posted its best comps in five years (+6.1%) on computing and AI glasses and raised FY27, Dollar Tree raised and gapped +11.5%, while Burlington cut on warm weather and freight. Housing remains the pressure point: mortgage rates are 7.28% despite 145bp of Fed cuts, commercial real estate activity fell 14% in October, and housing price expectations dropped sharply. Energy is split — crude under pressure on surplus and Libya's pipeline restart (helpful for CPI) while European gas and Japanese power prices spike on cold, keeping LNG and power-demand narratives alive. The portfolio's defensive-value, insurance-and-healthcare core is positioned on the right side of this rotation; the vulnerable sleeves are Masco (housing/rates) and, to a lesser degree, FedEx and Delta if tariffs bite volumes.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: a two-front de-rating. Rate-hike risk is being priced into the long end (5-year auction, PCE this week) at the same moment the AI capex complex loses its marginal buyer — the Huang-return squeeze lasted one session and the semis/hardware tape is gapping down 7-16%. Add a tariff announcement that could land today on China, EU and Japan. Expect continued multiple compression in Technology and high-beta AI adjacents, continued outperformance of Staples, Health Care, Utilities, insurance and Real Estate, a firm dollar, and gold chopping sideways around $3,600 as real-rate pressure offsets safe-haven bid. Breadth stays narrow but leadership is defensive, not cyclical.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: regime is Reflation (35.6, rising) bleeding into Stagflation (29.5, rising), with Goldilocks collapsing (-9.3). That favors pricing power, short-duration cash flows, hard assets and energy security over long-duration growth stories. A Fed that hikes into a 7.3% mortgage market will crush rate-sensitive housing and CRE while leaving nominal-GDP-linked earners (insurers reinvesting at higher yields, value retail, healthcare distributors) intact. The AI build-out does not stop, but it gets financed at higher spreads — SpaceX's bond hangover and the private-credit tug of war are the tell. Expect the market to separate AI companies with cash-funded capex from those with capital-markets-funded capex, violently.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: capital is being repriced away from infinite-duration narratives toward physical, metered, contracted cash flows — electricity, grid, nuclear, LNG, defense, rare earths and reshored industrial capacity. Electricity becomes the binding constraint on AI and on households simultaneously (cooling demand now overtaking heating demand globally; Japanese power at 2022 highs). Trade is fragmenting into blocs (China-ASEAN FTA 3.0, EU limits on Chinese hybrids, German industrials building a rare-earth trading house), which permanently raises the cost of goods and the value of supply-chain control. Structurally higher nominal rates mean the 2010s equity-duration trade does not return; the durable winners are owners of scarce physical capacity and of the balance sheets that finance it.

short_term: Households are spending confidently on discrete, deflationary technology (Best Buy's best comps in five years, AI glasses and computing demand) while trading down on consumables — Dollar Tree raising guidance into 'early holiday demand' is the same consumer, different wallet.

Savers are being pushed back into bonds and cash: long-duration Treasury flows are increasing, foreign bond inflows are returning, and retail is reading '401(k) millionaire counts are dropping' — the wealth-effect feedback loop is turning negative at the margin.

Homebuyers are capitulating on timing rather than price: 7.28% mortgages after 145bp of Fed cuts have broken the 'wait for the cut' heuristic, and search interest is shifting to 'housing market crash' and local market queries.
Firms are rationing AI deployment for liability reasons, not capability reasons — Signal, United Airlines and banks limiting customer-facing AI agents marks the start of an agent-governance phase.

Anxiety is migrating to data security and energy bills: cybersecurity attention is +65% vs 28d with 'data breach settlement/lawsuit payout' queries surging, and 'electricity bill assistance/calculator' queries are rising — people are experiencing inflation as a utility bill.
Retail speculators are being conditioned by a 31%-then--5% Nvidia round trip and an IPO that broke issue price; risk appetite for narrative equity is being trained down fast.
long_term: Security — physical, digital and energy — is becoming a recurring household and corporate budget line rather than a discretionary purchase; drone-warfare and breach-remediation literacy is entering mainstream search behaviour.

People increasingly buy compute and intelligence as a consumer good (AI glasses, local devices) rather than only as a cloud subscription, pushing value toward edge hardware retail and device replacement cycles.

Mobility preference is shifting from ownership to summoned autonomy (robotaxi query surge, Las Vegas-centred), which over a decade reduces household vehicle capex and raises demand for fleet-grade power and service infrastructure.
Housing demand is being redirected from purchase to renovation, rental and multigenerational arrangements as the mortgage channel stays impaired — repair-and-remodel beats new-build formation.
Health is being managed continuously rather than episodically (devices, diagnostics, metabolic monitoring), making healthcare a defensive growth staple rather than a cyclical service.
Attention and status are consolidating into live, communal, physical experiences (Super Bowl in IMAX) even as everyday media fragments — scarcity of shared moments is the monetizable asset.

what_changed_since_yesterday: No prior brief exists; this is the baseline. The following are the day-over-day moves in the tape itself.
The Jensen Huang return trade fully reversed: a 31% Nvidia gain and the Nasdaq's best day since April 2025 gave way to a 5%+ decline and a broad tech slide within 24 hours.
Anthropic broke below its $83 IPO price for the first time — the first hard evidence that the public market's bid for pure-play AI has a floor below issue.

Fed expectations shifted decisively hawkish: Williams would not rule out back-to-back hikes and said higher rates are likely over time; Ackman responded that a December hike could cause a recession and called for a 3% inflation target.
Hardware guidance broke down across the board overnight: ADI -15.7%, HPE -14.6%, DELL -11.3%, CRDO -10.4%, AMBA -9.9%, MRVL -7.6%, NTAP -5.9% pre-market.

The consumer surprised to the upside in two places at once — CB confidence 103.3 vs 92.5 expected, and Best Buy's best comps in five years with a guidance raise — while Dollar Tree raised and gapped +11.5% and Burlington cut.
Tariff risk moved from background to imminent: multiple outlets report new tariffs on China, the EU and Japan could be announced as soon as today.
Oil fell on supply surplus and Libya's pipeline reopening, pulling Treasury yields lower on the day even as the hawkish Fed narrative strengthened — a genuine tension in the inflation outlook.
Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed, pharma's largest deal in three years, re-opening large-cap pharma M&A.
Insider cluster buying clustered in physical-economy names: MP ($3.57M), WMB ($651k), CTVA ($523k), ETN ($316k), plus notable buys at AKAM, BG, PLD, BA, ELV and WY.
